title: Islam: one God
hook: the declaration of faith: there is no god but God, and Muhammad is God's messenger (Quran 112)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Lent, and ashes on the forehead. Your line was forty days. Did you keep your one small fast? Day two hundred sixty-seven, and a new visit: Islam.

A baby is born in a hospital in Cairo, or Jakarta, or Birmingham, Alabama. Within minutes, in many Muslim families, a father or grandfather leans close to the newborn's ear and softly speaks the call to prayer. So among the first words that baby ever hears is a sentence about God. And at the other end of life, families gathered at a bedside hope the same sentence will be among the last words spoken. First breath to last, one sentence frames it all. Today, on our visit to Islam: the shahada.
screen: `A NEWBORN, A WHISPER IN THE EAR.` → `A BEDSIDE, THE LAST WORDS.` → `THE SHAHADA.`

segments.voice: Shahada means witness, or testimony. It's the declaration at the heart of Islam, naming God and the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him: la ilaha illa Allah, Muhammad rasul Allah. There is no god but God, and Muhammad is the messenger of God. Allah is simply the Arabic word for God; Arab Christians use it too. The shahada has two halves. The first is about God: that God is one, with no partner and no rival. Muslims call this oneness tawhid, and it's the center of everything else. The second is about the Prophet: that he is God's messenger, bringing the Qur'an. Saying the shahada sincerely, with understanding, is how a person becomes Muslim. It's the first of the five pillars of Islam, and it's repeated in every call to prayer, five times a day, from minarets around the world. The Qur'an puts God's oneness most memorably in one of its shortest chapters, surah one hundred twelve. In Marmaduke Pickthall's 1930 translation: "Say: He is Allah, the One! Allah, the eternally Besought of all! He begetteth not nor was begotten. And there is none comparable unto Him." Four short lines. In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet is reported to have said this little chapter equals a third of the Qur'an, and many Muslims recite it every day. Notice the shape: first a negation, no god, and then an affirmation, but God. Many Muslim teachers say the negation clears the ground, all the false centers a life can have, money, status, fear, and the affirmation leaves only one. One.
screen: `SHAHADA — WITNESS, TESTIMONY.` · `NO GOD BUT GOD: TAWHID.` · `MUHAMMAD, THE MESSENGER.` · `SAY: HE IS ALLAH, THE ONE.` · then, large: `ONE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: sit with the word one. Breathe in, and let the mind be busy as it is. Breathe out, and quietly say, one. Each time a thought pulls at you, a worry, a plan, a craving, notice it, and come back: one. If you're Muslim, you might hold the shahada itself. If not, just let one be the only word in the room. The bell holds the time.
Shahada. Witness: there is no god but God, and Muhammad is the messenger of God. The first pillar of Islam. Today's word.
Your line: one. Today, when your attention splits ten ways, pick one thing and give it all of you. Day two hundred sixty-seven.

howItsDone: Muslims say the shahada in every daily prayer and hear it in every call to prayer; many whisper the call to prayer to a newborn and hope to say the shahada as their last words.

trapdoor: what you thought: a Muslim creed.
what it means: the testimony that there is no god but God and Muhammad is God's messenger; saying it sincerely makes one Muslim.
what a scholar hears: la ilaha illa Allah, negation then affirmation; tawhid, and surah al-Ikhlas (112), 'sincerity', a third of the Qur'an.

Shia Muslims add phrases to the adhan and many add a statement about Ali; the core shahada is shared. A Keeper may want this noted.
